stem.en: An electric bell is sealed inside a glass bell jar and connected to a vacuum pump. You pump until the jar holds a near vacuum. You can see the hammer striking the gong as clearly as you like.

text.en: The sound is now a whisper, because the thin air left in the jar carries it only weakly.
Almost no sound can be heard, because the hammer cannot work against so little material.
Almost no sound can be heard, because nothing is left between the gong and your ear to carry it.
The sound is exactly as loud, because the gong itself is still moving and a moving gong is enough.

explanation.en: The bell is unchanged - you can see the hammer still striking the gong - so the source is still making its vibration. What has gone is the air between the gong and your ear. Sound needs a material medium to cross, and a vacuum supplies none, so the sound cannot reach you at all.

hints.en: Two things changed in that jar: what is inside it, and what you can see the bell doing. Which of those two explains why the sound went?
The hammer has not slowed down. So the missing part is not the source - it is the route.
